comparator.name: Mathematics (Wiskunde)
comparator.sourceNotes: Controlling adopted Dutch OER articles 7.3–7.5: 54 EC first-year required plus 6 EC free; 24 EC later common courses; selected Wiskunde line 36 EC (18 prescribed + 18 restricted, at least 6 from year three); 48 EC later genuinely free; thesis 12 EC. Total 54+6+24+36+48+12=180. First-year Reële Analyse, Statistiek and Wiskunde Practicum follow the formal current table; Introduction to Data Science is not added as another current compulsory unit. RADAr language support is required at 0 EC and not counted as an additional credited component. Writing Skills in Academia is selected from the paired writing alternatives, counted once. The first-listed Wiskunde line is selected neutrally; its restricted choices are the first two eligible year-two rows and first year-three row: Complexe Analyse, Maattheorie, Inleiding PDV, each 6 EC. Later free space remains generic. The ordinary domestic single-degree route retains Bachelor Seminar; conditional waivers for education minor, mobility or double bachelor are not assumed. Article 8.1 permits the old 48-EC line only for entrants in 2024–2025 or earlier, which is not this route. Public year pages all say indicative 2027–2028; their old 48-EC line and 36-EC free-space narrative does not override the current OER. The formal current pathway is reconstructed without asserting guaranteed future timetable availability. Current replacement OER version1.1 dated6October2026 retains this curriculum; amendment concerns whole-exam exemptions rather than subtests. Current thesis catalogue: prior compulsory first-two-year courses (Voorkennis); individual staff-supervised research or literature thesis, interim and final presentations and active peer participation. Osiris Zaak approval/intake and two approved assessors; ordinary spring offering, autumn only by organiser agreement. Normal BSA39EC; mandatory RADAr participation0EC, pass not required, prior-test exemption. Bachelor composition approval three months before graduation. No general compulsory international mobility or internship.

alternatives.concept: Develop calculus, algebra, probability and numerical methods through mathematical algorithms, statistical learning and economic modelling. This is the closest available computational response to the generic Mathematics target; it retains the visible gaps in its selected pure-mathematics line. The shared mathematics backbone covers methods, linear algebra, multivariable calculus, numerical equations, signals and probability; it does not reproduce the selected pure-mathematics sequence or its compulsory thesis.

alternatives.concept: Combine calculus, linear algebra, probability, numerical algorithms and statistical learning with biomedical measurements, medical-image analysis and quantitative pharmacological models. Biological and anatomical study supplies the subject knowledge needed to interpret those applications; this is not a pure-mathematics or clinical Medicine curriculum. The shared mathematics backbone covers methods, linear algebra, multivariable calculus, numerical equations, signals and probability; it does not reproduce the selected pure-mathematics sequence or its compulsory thesis.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Three complete, substantively distinct programmes pass. Medical modelling is supported by the exact target interest and official programme description, explicit medical imaging in Image Processing & Computer Vision, and quantitative pharmacological models in Pharmacology. Biological foundations and laboratory measurements make that related response coherent; a dedicated named mathematical-medicine sequence is not required. The physics/astronomy candidate still lacks a cumulative physics/astronomy sequence, and the education candidate lacks mathematics-specific teaching/didactics content; neither supplies a credible separate complete programme. Pure-mathematics gaps remain explicit in all alternatives. The pure/theoretical-mathematics generator is rejected because the defining analysis, abstract algebra, topology and measure/PDE sequence is absent; it is not owned by the applied closest option.

notes.text: Radboud’s selected Wiskunde line includes a deeper sequence in real and complex analysis, abstract algebra, topology, measure theory and partial differential equations. These UCR programmes instead combine mathematical methods with computation, statistics and economic or biomedical applications; they do not reproduce that pure-mathematics sequence.

Radboud requires an individual 12 EC mathematics thesis with supervision, interim and final presentations, and active peer participation. Optional UCR independent research is additional, approval-dependent and outside the displayed 180 EC. A UCR composition does not establish degree equivalence, a teaching qualification or admission to a particular master.

audience.programmeDescription: Radboud Mathematics develops abstract mathematical reasoning and practical modelling. Its ordinary bachelor combines calculus, analysis, linear and abstract algebra, programming and probability with a chosen mathematical line, open study space and an individual mathematics thesis. The comparison uses the Wiskunde line, including topology, rings and fields, differential equations and restricted advanced choices.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers three related directions built around mathematical methods, computation and statistics, with economic or biomedical applications. The economic direction adds substantive economic models and econometrics. The biomedical direction combines a mathematical backbone with biological foundations, medical image processing and quantitative pharmacology. These are qualified applied responses: real and complex analysis, abstract algebra, topology, measure theory and partial differential equations remain substantial gaps. General biology or business courses are subject foundations rather than replacements for that mathematics.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC comprises 54 EC required first-year courses,6 EC first-year free choice,24 EC later common courses,36 EC in the selected line,48 EC later free choice and a 12 EC individual thesis. The line includes 18 EC prescribed and 18 EC restricted choices, with at least 6 EC from year three. Optional minors, mobility and combined degrees are not universal requirements. Normal first-year study advice requires 39 EC, subject to applicable exceptions. RADAr language-test participation is required without extra credit; passing is not required. Thesis prior knowledge comprises the compulsory first-two-year courses. Topic approval, registration, two assessors and interim/final presentations with active peer participation apply. The thesis normally runs in spring. The chosen bachelor composition requires board approval before graduation.
